newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former president FW de KLerk knew that the Steyn report on defence force dirty tricks -- which he denied existing in writing -- had implicated current SA National Defence Force chief Georg Meiring and 60 top military officers in crimes, the truth commission alleged.
- Motor manufacturer Automakers Ltd share price shot up more than 37 percent on rumours that Japan's Nissan Motor Company and Italy's Fiat would acquire Sankorp's majority stake in the company.
- Government revenue was up a robust 17 percent in the first nine months of the fiscal year compared with the same period a year ago -- a sign that the economy is still healthy.

- The gold mines managed by Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd lifted taxed profit 21 percent to 333 million rand in the December quarter as gold production rose eight percent to 22,902 kg and a fragile calm was restored among disafffected workers.

- Anglo American Corporation of SA and Gencor Ltd have agreed to a comprehensive rationalisation of their groups' mineral rights which is expected to result in efficient and early exploitation of reserves in the Klerkdorp, Evander and Free State gold fields.

- Sun City, the multibillion-rand gambling, hotel and leisure complex in the North West Province, could be forced to close if the Gauteng government allocated its full allowances of gaming licences, Peter Bacon, the Sun International group managing director, said.

- Kolosus Holdings Ltd, the aggressive food group, was expected to announce its acquisition of Ladysmith Leathers, the motor vehicle leather producer, for about 50 million rand on Friday, market sources said on Thursday.
- Police have arrested eight "ruthless gangsters" linked to a series of rapes and armed robberies in Johannesburg, including recent brutal attacks on two families.
- South Africa has the highest number of rapes in the world, according to a quarterly report released by the Ministry of Safety and Security and the police.

- Former president FW de Klerk said he was astounded at Truth and Reconcillitaion Commission allegations that he had ignored recommendations made by General Pierre Steyn about unlawful activities by three top army generals.
